title: Rekor Commits to Mandatory Privacy Protections, Offering Communities a New Path to Adopt or Restore ALPR
summary: Rekor Commits to Mandatory Privacy Protections, Offering Communities a New Path to Adopt or Restore ALPR
body_markdown:
*Rekor Board Adopts Mandatory ALPR Privacy Standard for Law Enforcement Customers*


**COLUMBIA, Md., November 16, 2026 —** Rekor Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ: REKR) ("Rekor" or the "Company"), which builds trusted data, privacy, and security solutions for real-world video and sensor networks, today announced that its Board of Directors has formally adopted a mandatory privacy, security, and accountability standard for law enforcement customers of its Automated License Plate Recognition ("ALPR") services.


**This standard is not optional** . It is designed to preserve legitimate public safety alerts while restricting access to historical information about vehicles that are not on authorized hotlists. Rekor is establishing these rules voluntarily, rather than waiting for federal legislation, and will incorporate them into its agreements with law enforcement customers as management completes the necessary contractual and operational provisions.


*"Communities should not have to choose between effective policing and the privacy of ordinary motorists. We are setting a high bar for ourselves because someone in this industry needs to demonstrate that both objectives can be achieved. This is not about asking the public to trust a vendor. It is about operating under clear rules that the vendor cannot set aside to win a contract."*


— Robert A. Berman, Rekor Systems


Rekor's standard rests on three substantive safeguards: encryption and restricted reidentification of non-hotlist vehicle information; defined, purpose-based retention and deletion; and authentication of digital evidence through Born Authentic™. Mandatory two-factor authentication and prompt removal of former personnel's access provide additional security.


## A corporate standard with accountability


The Board's adoption makes these safeguards part of Rekor's operating requirements for law enforcement customers. Customer preference and competitive considerations will not justify exceptions to the standard. Management is responsible for finalizing contract terms, procedures, technical controls, and compliance oversight consistent with the Board's action.


*"There needs to be a judge between the police and the average citizen when officers seek access to ALPR-captured historical vehicle records. A useful framework should be technology-neutral and provide practical safeguards that any responsible ALPR vendor can implement. Rekor is taking an operational step now to show how those safeguards can work in the field, while continuing to welcome examination and input from policymakers, law enforcement and civil-liberties stakeholders."*


— Charles Degliomini, Executive Vice President of Government Affairs, Rekor Systems


## Preparing for a national framework


If Congress or a state enacts legislation governing ALPR in the future, Rekor will align its standards and operating practices with applicable federal law. The Company believes its board-approved requirements set a high standard today, without presuming to replace future legislation.


## Implementation and public discussion


The standard applies to law enforcement customers going forward. Rekor will honor all existing law enforcement customer contracts through their stated terms. When a contract expires, the agency may continue with Rekor under the new standard or choose a different provider; **Rekor will not renew an arrangement that excludes the mandatory requirements.** Agencies that want to adopt the standard sooner may work with Rekor on an appropriate amendment, subject to implementation readiness. Rekor also plans to host a public webinar for municipal leaders, law enforcement, policymakers, privacy advocates and other stakeholders, with scheduling and registration details to follow.


The full Board-adopted standard is set out below as a distinct policy section of this release.


## Rekor ALPR Privacy, Security and Accountability Standard


This standard governs law enforcement ALPR customer arrangements entered into following Board adoption, subject to implementation through Rekor's customer agreements and operating procedures. The following requirements are mandatory and are not discretionary customer options.


## Pillar 1 | Privacy by design — non-hotlist vehicle information


Rekor will protect identifying information associated with vehicles that do not generate a legally authorized hotlist alert through encryption and anonymization at the point of collection. Real-time alerts for vehicles on authorized law enforcement hotlists, including stolen vehicles, missing or endangered persons, and other authorized public safety purposes, will remain available.


Information associated with vehicles that do not generate an authorized alert will not be available for routine historical browsing, unrestricted tracking, or discretionary reidentification by law enforcement users or Rekor. Protected information may be reidentified only pursuant to a judicial warrant supported by probable cause, appropriately limited in scope and verified under the Company's warrant-handling procedures.


Police already use electronic warrant systems to request judicial review, with around-the-clock procedures available in some jurisdictions. An officer submits a sworn application explaining the evidence sought and the basis for probable cause. A judge reviews the facts, determines whether the search is justified and appropriately limited, and electronically returns an approved warrant. This process supports rapid investigations while preserving independent judicial oversight.


## Pillar 2 | Purpose-based incident retention and deletion


Rekor will apply defined retention and deletion requirements to routine observations and authorized incident-related records. Preservation must be tied to a legitimate, documented purpose, applicable legal requirements, and appropriate authorization. Retention will not be extended indefinitely merely because the technology permits it, and discretionary extensions without a lawful basis are prohibited.


Specific retention periods, incident classifications, legal-hold procedures and audit controls will be reflected in the operating standard and customer agreements as finalized by management.


## Pillar 3 | Authenticity and integrity of digital evidence


Rekor will incorporate Born Authentic™, its digital media authentication technology, into its ALPR evidence framework for supported media and workflows. The objective is to support independent verification of the authenticity and integrity of relevant images, video, and audio offered in investigations or judicial proceedings.


Implementation procedures will specify supported media, authentication points, recordkeeping and verification workflows.


## Mandatory system access controls


Two-factor authentication will be required for authorized users of Rekor's law enforcement ALPR systems and may not be disabled at the customer's discretion. Customer agencies must maintain current authorized-user records, use individual credentials where required, and promptly revoke access for personnel who retire, transfer, leave service, or otherwise cease to be authorized. Rekor will maintain associated administrative and audit procedures.


## Corporate accountability and non-waiver


These requirements are a formal Board-adopted corporate standard for law enforcement customer arrangements. Management shall implement and enforce the requirements through appropriate technical, administrative, and contractual controls. Commercial pressure, a customer preference, or a desire to secure or retain business does not justify waiving a requirement. Applicable laws and legally mandated preservation or disclosure obligations remain controlling.


## Relationship to future federal law


If Congress enacts legislation regulating ALPR technology, Rekor will review and align this standard and its operations with applicable federal requirements. Until then, Rekor voluntarily commits to the requirements set forth here for law enforcement customers.


## Existing customers and transition


Rekor will honor each existing law enforcement contract through its stated term. At expiration, the customer may elect to continue with Rekor under this standard or select another provider. Rekor will not renew a contract that waives the standard. Existing customers seeking earlier adoption may request appropriate contract amendments, subject to implementation readiness. Nothing here represents that all existing deployments have already transitioned.


## Public engagement


Rekor intends to make the standard available for public review and to host a webinar addressing the protections, their practical application and questions from stakeholders. Webinar details will be announced separately.
